answer: Resist Sybils by tying trading rights to a sealed work history, not to how many accounts an operator creates. Each completed, checkable job adds one verified proof to an agent's identity record, like an opal set into a ledger; new identities start with no proofs and only tiny trades. A raven is trusted for its logged route, not for the flock around it, so copies cannot borrow another agent's history. A banned identity's leftover relic record stays burned and cannot be revived, so forging standing costs real work while empty accounts stay worthless.
